chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Hamid, from Mus'ab ibn Abdullah al-Nawfali, from the one who raised it, who said:

A Bedouin arrived with his camels in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, sell these camels of mine for me.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'I am not a seller in the markets.' He said, 'So advise me.' He said to him, 'Sell this camel for such and such, and sell this she-camel for such and such,' until he described each of the camels from them.

So the Bedouin went out to the market and sold them, then he came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'By the One who sent you with the truth, they neither increased nor decreased by a dirham from what you told me. So accept my gift, O Messenger of Allah.' He said, 'No.' He said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' So he did not cease speaking to him until he said to him, 'Gift us a she-camel and do not make it a toy (or distraction).'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) handle commercial transactions and gifts from the Bedouins?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) unique economic role, distinguishing his guidance from mere market trading by offering precise valuation for each animal. The Bedouin’s insistence on gifting a she-camel highlights the spiritual value of the Prophet’s counsel, a theme resonating with Quranic verses on divine guidance and the Prophet's intercession. In Shia tradition, this narrative underscores the Prophet’s comprehensive knowledge and the merit of accepting his practical advice in worldly matters.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Mus’ab Bin Abdullah Al nowfaly, from the one who raised it who said,

‘A Bedouin came over upon a camel of his, in the era of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he said to him<sup>saww</sup>, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Sell this camel of mine for me’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> am not a seller in the market’. He said, ‘So indicate to me (how to sell)’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said to him: ‘Sell this camel with such and such, and sell this she-camel with such and such’, until he<sup>saww</sup> had described each of the camels from it.

So the Bedouin went out to the market, and he sold them. Then he came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘By the One<sup>azwj</sup> Who Sent you<sup>saww</sup> with the Truth, there was neither increase one Dirham nor reduced by one Dirham from what you<sup>saww</sup> had said to me, therefore accept my gift O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘No’. He said, ‘Yes, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’ So he did not cease to speak to him<sup>saww</sup> until he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Gift to me a she-camel and do not make it leave its young’.
en.sarwar: 53. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from al-‘Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from a man from Mandal ibn Ali al-‘Anziy from Muhammad ibn Mutarrif from Misma’ from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who has said the following:

“’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘When Allah becomes angry with a people on whom He has not sent any suffering, He makes their prices to become costly, shortens their life span, takes away profit from their trade, their fruits do not become clean, their canals do not over-flow and He withholds their rain and makes their wicked ones to dominate them.’”
